verdict: Slightly better on process, worse on trust. Billing, proactive reports and new-staff introductions all improved, and Sarah moved to active, the first live account to leave at_risk in weeks. But on 10/11 we told eleven clients in writing that their relaunched link-in-bio domain 'won't get flagged and it's completely safe'. Within two days it flagged Lilia, Sarah (twice) and Vale, and a recovered Barbara backup went down. We pulled it on 10/15 with no apology, and six of the eleven were never told it was pulled. Meanwhile last week's open items (Liza's 2FA incident, Barbara's 9/14 message, every churned client's exit) have not moved at all.

fires.why: On 10/11 Mayson sent the same message to Alanna, Barbara, Haileigh, Lauren Blake, Lauryn, Lilia, Liza, Mila, Sarah Lloyd, Sarah, Shayna and Vale: domain is back, 'new technology', 'won't get flagged and it's completely safe'. Lilia was flagged 10/12 ('The link I got flagged me yesterday'). Sarah was flagged 10/13 and again 10/16. Vivek confirmed Vale's was flagged 10/13. A Barbara backup went down within 21 hours of carrying it. Vale now says 'Losing money :(' and is comparing notes with Shayna ('Shayna said it got flagged for Lilia'). On 10/15 at 22:00 Mayson told six of them to remove it and switched them to a direct link, with no explanation and no apology. Alanna, Haileigh, Lauren Blake, Lauryn, Mila and Sarah Lloyd got no takedown notice in the group, so their bios may still point at a dead or flagged domain. Haileigh's is the same domain that got two of her accounts restricted in June. Clients are now talking to each other about it, so this is a trust problem across the whole book, not one account at a time.

systemic_fix: Test before you promise, and close what you broke. Two rules. (1) Nothing that touches a client's Instagram (bio link, domain, vendor, login) goes live until it has run 48 hours on a test account, and nobody writes 'won't get flagged' or 'completely safe'. We say what we've tested. (2) When we reverse a change, everyone who got the original message gets the reversal, with the reason and an apology if we caused harm. This week eleven clients were promised safety, four got hurt within two days, and six were never told it was pulled.
team_broadcast:
Team, one rule change effective today, and it comes from this week's link-in-bio rollout.

On the 11th we told eleven clients their new domain 'won't get flagged and it's completely safe'. Within two days it flagged Lilia, Sarah and Vale, and a Barbara backup went down. On the 15th we pulled it, but only six of the eleven were told. Clients are now comparing notes with each other about it.

So from now on:
1. Nothing goes into a client's bio, and no new vendor touches an account, until it has run 48 hours on a test account.
2. Never write 'won't get flagged' or 'completely safe'. Say what we tested and what we're watching.
3. If we roll something back, every client who got the first message gets the rollback, the same day, with the reason.
4. Never ask for a password or 2FA code in a group chat. Access goes through a private channel only.

Mayson, please confirm by end of day which of Alanna, Haileigh, Lauren Blake, Lauryn, Mila and Sarah Lloyd still have the old domain live. I'm messaging all eleven myself.
pattern: The things we do on a schedule are getting better: invoices go out with a heads-up and no threats, earnings reports exist now, new staff introduce themselves. Clients have noticed, and now they talk to each other about it (Vale quoting Shayna about Lilia). The churn signature (fast payment, warm thank-yous, zero asks) now fits Liza, Lauren Blake and Haileigh. Sarah went the other way because she got numbers and the call she asked for.
